findings: Boundary review: 13/69 sampled units (19%) are fragments, cut clusters, or turn-alignment failures; these are not clean Q&A evidence.

Most frequent class corrections: direct_interview_candidate -> rhetorical_candidate (21); unclear_dialogue_context -> direct_interview_candidate (10); unclear_dialogue_context -> rhetorical_candidate (10); unclear_dialogue_context -> secondary_report (5).

The expanded Kryon sample contains many speaker-posed or audience-ventriloquized questions in solo monologue; address terms such as 'dear one' and 'you might say' are not sufficient evidence of a two-party interview.
Quoted dialogue in anecdotes and practitioner-relayed entity speech remains secondary_report; direct audience Q&A is promoted only where the bounded text shows a responsive exchange.
Review allocation spans 13 claimed-entity labels; Kryon contributes 37 items and Ryokah/Sassani 10. This is a stratified diagnostic sample, not a population estimate.

Automatic answer-window states in the sample: {'interrupted_by_next_question': 22, 'complete_line_cap': 46, 'no_answer_end_of_transcript': 1}. Orientation and family labels describe text shape only, not answer truth or consensus.

tiny.en ASR errors, long multi-sentence segments, and absent diarization limit speaker/addressee inference. Review is ai_agent_review, not human annotation; every verdict binds to the current question hash and source metadata; humanValidated stays false.
reviewSummary.caution: AI review, not human annotation; humanValidated stays false. Reviewed classes refine textual heuristics only; no speaker attribution, truth or consensus assessment.
